overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting notice only on the municipal website instead of in or on the town hall, and by discouraging a member of the public from audio-recording an open meeting. Ordered immediate and future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the board failed to post proper notice for its May 26, 2012 meeting, which was posted only on the municipal website.
allegations.key_passage: Because Middlefield has not notified the Attorney General that it has adopted an alternative notice posting method, the Board should have posted its notice "in or on the municipal building in which the clerk's office is located."

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the board unlawfully prohibited an individual from audio-recording the May 26, 2012 open meeting, after a 2-1 vote asking her not to tape.
allegations.key_passage: because the Law unequivocally states that "any person may make a video or audio recording of an open session meeting of a public body," it is improper for a public body to discourage an individual who wishes to record a meeting from doing so.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the law.
